AboutPage.title: Who We Are
AboutPage.subtitle: AOSSIE (Australian Open Source Software Innovation and Education) is a registered not-for-profit organization (ABN: 32 743 493 466) dedicated to the research and development of free and open-source software as well as to the education of the principles and methods of open-source software development. Our projects are always innovation-focused and frequently research-intensive. All of our software libraries and applications are 100% free and open-source.

Timeline.title: Our Journey
Timeline.subtitle: Over a decade of empowering contributors to make a positive impact.
Timeline.m1Desc: Three of AOSSIE's four initial projects (Skeptik/Scavenger, Carbon Footprint for Google Maps, and Mind the Word) were implemented by Dr. Bruno Woltzenlogel Paleo and began participating in GSoC under the CSE@TU-Wien organization.
Timeline.m2Desc: Dr. Bruno Woltzenlogel Paleo founded the Australian Open Source Software Innovation and Education (AOSSIE).
Timeline.m3Desc: AOSSIE participated in Google Summer of Code independently for the first time, mentoring students globally. The Agora electronic voting project became AOSSIE's flagship fourth project.
Timeline.m4Desc: AOSSIE was registered as a not-for-profit organization in Australia (ABN: 32 743 493 466) under the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission (ACNC).
Timeline.m5Desc: AOSSIE started vastly expanding its ecosystem with new projects using blockchains and AI.
Timeline.m6Title: 10th largest GSoC Organization in the World
Timeline.m6Desc: AOSSIE became the 10th largest organization in the world by both number of completed GSoC projects per year and total number of completed projects, among a cohort of 600+ organizations.

ApplyPage.title: How to Apply & Contribute
ApplyPage.subtitle: Follow our step-by-step roadmap to get involved with AOSSIE open-source projects and prepare a competitive GSoC proposal.
ApplyPage.s1Desc: Join the AOSSIE community on Discord and connect with developers, mentors, and maintainers. Our Discord server is the central hub to ask questions, share project ideas, and get support throughout the Google Summer of Code application process.
ApplyPage.s2Desc: Explore AOSSIE GitHub repositories and pick beginner-friendly or good-first-issues. Submitting code or documentation pull requests showcases your technical understanding and willingness to collaborate with project maintainers.
ApplyPage.s3Desc: Select a project idea from our GSoC Ideas List or propose your own innovative feature. Expand the idea into a detailed proposal detailing your technical approach, implementation architecture, timeline milestones, and deliverables.
ApplyPage.s4Desc: Share your proposal draft with our dedicated mentors on Discord or GitHub. Experienced mentors will review your implementation timeline, provide architectural feedback, and help you refine your application to maximize your selection chances.
ApplyPage.s5Desc: Submit your finalized PDF application to the official Google Summer of Code portal before the deadline. Double-check all required deliverables, milestone breakdowns, and contact information. Good luck!
